newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower on profit-taking.

text.p: French stocks opened weaker on Wednesday, pressured by concerns about long-term interest rate trends that fuelled profit-taking, traders said.

"A lot of analysts are unclear where the market's going from here," said Olivier Blitz at IFF Bourse. He said the bourse's underlying upward trend looked intact, particularly if the futures contract held above 2,670 points.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 14.06 points, or 0.52 percent, at 2,672.09 at 0930 GMT. The CAC-40 March futures contract was 13 points lower at 2,682.
Volume was a light 785 million francs in the first 30 minutes of trading.

Shares in building materials group Lafarge rose 1.63 percent to 373.50 francs after the group reported net attributable profit of 1.85 billion francs, which while down from 2.35 billion in 1995, was well received by the market. Lafarge also said it expected 1997 sales to rise more than 10 percent.

Car shares were mixed. Renault's stock was up 0.83 percent at 134.10 francs, recouping part of Tuesday's fall of over four percent, but PSA Peugeot Citroen shares were 1.3 percent lower at 621 francs. Some clients are being told to steer clear.

"People are rejoicing over job-reduction plans, but they're being announced in a context of low growth in 1997 and margin erosion because of over-capacity. More cars are built than can be sold. If people want to stay in the sector, we're advising them to switch to suppliers," a broker said.
Shares in building group Bouygues fell 2.52 percent to 581 francs, pressured by a report in the satirical weekly Canard Enchaine of a Swiss probe in its activities, brokers said.
